chapter_title: Concerning the Eighteen Great Thrones of all the Fathers
chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by the oldest teaching layer — a systematic enumeration of 18 cosmic thrones (9 in the eternal realm, 9 in the material world). The substrate is remarkably intact with minimal editorial overlay. The only significant editorial intervention is in ¶17, where the ninth worldly throne is identified with Mani's own apostolic seat ('the apostle who has come to you at this time'). The devotional closure 'for ever and ever, amen' in ¶11 is the only exhortation. The editorial fatigue pattern is confirmed: institutional vocabulary only appears in the final third (¶10, ¶17). The teaching structure — numbered hierarchy mapping cosmic beings to cosmic positions and functions — is classic cosmological-correspondential substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: Eighteen [great thrones for all the fathers] exist and are appointed, which are established in eighteen places! While there are nine among them [appointed in] the outer aeons, they exist [i]n all the worlds of the damage.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'Once again he speaks to his disciples:' — dialogue frame attribution formula.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Frame formula wraps a substantive cosmological statement that defines the entire teaching structure (18 thrones, 9+9 distribution). The structural overview is substrate; the attribution is editorial frame.

paragraphs.core_text: The first throne is the throne of the Father, the God of [trut]h, the King of the aeons of greatness, the one who exists; who is established [...] he alone, in his own essen[c]e, [...] apart. This is the first throne [...] the one that surpasses all the thrones.
paragraphs.temporal_note: First enumeration unit. Maps first throne → highest cosmic entity (the Father). Both sides stay within the cosmic system. Lacunae suggest damaged manuscript but the teaching structure is clear.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.82⟩ The second throne is that of the [gl]orious Mother of Life. She is the origin of all the emanations that have come to this world.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second enumeration unit. Throne → cosmic entity (Mother of Life) → cosmic function (origin of emanations). Pure cosmological mapping. High substrate score (26.92) confirms.

paragraphs.core_text: The third throne is constructed for the father, the First Man. He is the one who humiliated the entire first enmity, which existed in the worlds of Darkness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third enumeration unit. Throne → First Man → cosmic function (defeating the primordial Enmity in the worlds of Darkness). 'The entire first enmity' is a cosmic-process term. Capitalized 'Darkness' as it functions as a cosmic domain.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth throne is that of the Beloved of the Lights, the great honoured Beloved of the aeons of greatness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fourth enumeration unit. Highest substrate score in the chapter (35.0). Pure cosmic entity identification with no functional description — just the being and its cosmic position.

paragraphs.core_text: The fifth throne is that of the glorious Great Builder; the great architect who built the new aeon for a newness, for [a ...] for [the] fathers of light; also for a place of binding and a prison for the enemy and his powers.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fifth enumeration unit. Throne → Great Builder → cosmic function (constructing the new aeon, creating a binding-place for the enemy). Both sides stay within the cosmic system. 'Place of binding and a prison for the enemy' is cosmic architecture, not metaphor for earthly institutions.

paragraphs.core_text: [The sixth thro]n[e] is that of the Living Spirit, the [glorious] mighty one, he who bore up the First Man out from the [land of Darkness]; who also set in order and constructed the world [s ...] both for a cleansing of the light, [and] for a binding [of the] powers of the enmity.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Sixth enumeration unit. Throne → Living Spirit → dual cosmic function (rescue of First Man from the land of Darkness; world-construction for light-cleansing and enmity-binding). This is systematic cosmic-process description.

paragraphs.core_text: The seventh th[rone is] that of the Third Ambassador, the king of the zone, also the master of all advices.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Seventh enumeration unit. Throne → Third Ambassador → cosmic titles (king of the zone, master of all advices). 'Zone' is cosmic geography; 'advices' is a cosmic-faculty term.

paragraphs.core_text: The eighth throne is that of Jesus the Splendour, who [is] the releaser and redeemer [of] all souls.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Eighth enumeration unit. 'Jesus the Splendour' is the cosmic Manichaean entity (not the historical Jesus), functioning as the releaser of souls — a cosmic process. Both sides of the mapping stay within the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: The ninth throne is the throne of the great M[ind, he to whom] all the churches shall gather; and all the [life] that will be purified from the world returns to him.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Ninth enumeration unit completing the first set. 'Churches' (ekklesia) here functions cosmically as 'assemblies of light' — the Great Mind's function is gathering purified life, confirmed by the parallel clause 'all the life that will be purified from the world returns to him.' Both sides stay within the cosmic system. Institutional score (6.25) is a minor flag; the word 'churches' triggers it but the mapping is cosmic. Some uncertainty remains.

paragraphs.core_text: These are the nine thrones of ho[no]u[r] appointed in the outer aeo[ns], <which are established> for the fathers of the glorious realm; [in the kingdom of the King of] Honour.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'for ever and ever, amen' — devotional closure formula (exhortation layer). The seam flag is a false positive here; the summary statement is structural, not an editorial extension.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Structural summary closing the first set of nine thrones. The summary mirrors the transitional paragraph 12 that opens the second set — both are structural markers within the enumeration. Only the liturgical 'for ever and ever, amen' is late.

paragraphs.core_text: In contrast, these are the other nine thrones that are appointed in this world of the zone.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Structural transition introducing the second set of nine thrones. 'This world of the zone' is cosmic geography. This mirrors the opening statement in ¶1 about the 9+9 structure and is part of the teaching's organizational skeleton.

paragraphs.core_text: Three thrones in the ship of [the d]ay: one is that of the Ambassador, the second i[s that of] the Great Spirit, the third is that of the Living Spirit.
paragraphs.temporal_note: First triad of the worldly thrones. 'Ship of the day' is cosmic vessel/geography. Maps three cosmic entities to their thrones in the solar ship. High substrate score (16.67).

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.83⟩ Once again, there are another three in the ship that [belongs to the night]: the first is the throne of Jesus the Splendour, [the second is that of] the First Man, the third is tha[t of the Virgin of] Light. These six thrones are established in the two ships.
paragraphs.temporal_note: 'Once again' here is a continuation marker within the teaching structure (not the dialogue frame formula 'Once again the enlightener speaks'). Second triad: three entities in the lunar ship. The summary 'These six thrones are established in the two ships' is a structural sub-total within the enumeration.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, the seventh throne is established in the seventh firmament. The great King of Honour sits upon it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Seventh worldly throne. Maps cosmic position (seventh firmament) → cosmic entity (King of Honour). High substrate score (22.22). Pure cosmological mapping.

paragraphs.core_text: The eighth throne is established in the atmosphere. The Judge of truth sits upon it, he who judges all mankind. Three paths shall be distinguished before him: one to death, one to life, on[e] to the mingling.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Eighth worldly throne. Maps cosmic position (atmosphere) → cosmic entity (Judge of truth) → cosmic function (tripartite judgment). The 'three paths' (death, life, mingling) are cosmic destinies within the system, not contemporary application. 'Judges all mankind' is cosmic function, not institutional content.

paragraphs.core_text: The ninth throne appointed and established is for the [a]postle.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'in the holy church. The apostle who has come to you at this time sits up[on it]; thus, [as jud]ge of righteousn[ess]. They shall proclaim [true] judgem[ent] every t[ime]!' — institutional application identifying Mani as currently occupying this throne. 'Holy church,' 'come to you at this time,' and direct address all reach outside the cosmic system into the editor's contemporary world.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The enumeration REQUIRES a ninth worldly throne; the substrate core identifies this position for 'the apostle' (a cosmic function completing the hierarchy). Everything from 'in the holy church' onward is the institutional layer mapping this cosmic position to Mani's own authority. Gardner synopsis confirms: 'Mani illustrates to his audience that he is now occupying it.' The institutional score (12.82) is the highest in the chapter, confirming the layer shift.

paragraphs.core_text: Th[ese] are the [nin]e great [th]ro[nes ...] that are established in this world of [...] of the glorious realm, the one that the [... ...] honour them [... ...] and the [...].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Closing summary of the second set of nine thrones, structurally parallel to ¶11's summary of the first set. Heavily damaged by lacunae but the structural function is clear. No devotional closure ('amen') survives — either it was absent or lost to damage.
